notes.title: Sierra Madre Dev Blog 9-23-2022
notes.content:
[h1]Pre-Release Content and Images[/h1]

Please understand that the material discussed herein is part of the unreleased CORE Release Update and does not reflect the current version of the game that is now available on the Steam store. The CORE Release Update is a complete overall of the existing game and has not been released at this date. We appreciate your patience and continued interest.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33892364/8232472ca7cf3646029be49a89581c37e6d9c302.png[/img]

[h1]Changes to Gameplay[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33892364/4482d8893c6c53b0f81087311818528436debb78.png[/img]

The game’s gameplay has received a significant overhaul. In the current version of the game, the goal is survival where the player must secure resources to maintain their health, nutrition levels, hydration, etc. This will be eliminated. In the CORE Release Update, food and drink will only affect health level and gameplay will be driven by a faction-based scoring system.

New factions have been created to represent the struggle of life on the frontier. Players will be part of the pioneers looking to settle the area known as the Homesteader faction. Peaceful Native Americans, trappers, other frontiersman, and livestock are also part of this faction. This faction, a rival ranching faction, two outlaw factions, a hostile Native American faction, and multiple wildlife factions (bears, wolves, etc.) will all compete to be the last surviving faction.

Factions earn or lose score based on Faction Missions. These missions will be spawned by rival factions and require the player to complete a task or series of tasks. If the player successfully completes the mission the Homesteader (player) faction gains score and the rival faction loses score; however, if the player fails to complete the mission (or dies while attempting to complete the mission) that rival faction gains score. Random missions also will exist on the map. These do not contribute to the score of any faction but will offer the player with higher personal rewards than a faction mission. The player shall look on the map for available missions and select one to activate the mission. Only active missions may be completed.

[h1]Changes to the Map[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33892364/e552e8d62cd9a25cc9b4c80182bfb15cb76f0e68.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33892364/ad38a5f3228677c4ebff67586bc49b262d4c749a.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33892364/fec8b25f4611b827189a5e9e4472bfd28b895f19.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33892364/90a4ba5bb5cd49b59bd45ef1f1f42d09b8fc53ab.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33892364/34dfc3c7cea04559f73bbe5d7cebc420c31c9a71.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33892364/68f33c5e3247e87c4199d5d7fdd11ab649a403a5.png[/img]

The new map features a more consistent environment with the desert being eliminated. The map still has diversity in the terrain and plants with flat areas and grasslands transitioning into hills, small mountains, and canyons; further, greater detail has been added to the ground texture and within each map area. We are hoping that this will create a more realistic feel.

[h1]Changes to Character Assets[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33892364/6338fafcbff92702ad3eff0319f3e61969d20b45.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33892364/1ceb6e97ace1ffc007734d1ae93e07036c876e3a.png[/img]

Since our last blog post, we have made modifications to our character models. We have added more realistic hair and facial hair and made some changes to outfits as well. We have also incorporated cloth physics on certain clothing and hairs. Players will now be able to choose from several faces, outfits, hairstyles and hats, and be able to select gender and skin tone.

[h1]Changes to Weapons Artwork[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33892364/ae06d06e1379fdcb7ce031877a7d9ef9643ee17d.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33892364/3c5d50ce6d6e93e932fe24303572e096ab469a6f.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33892364/6ee63d7062a0e16613640bf1ae85df303cb76fe8.png[/img]

We have reworked the weapon artwork and created several variants of repeaters including a Model 60, Model 66, Model 73, and Model 76 to name a few. More weapons are in the pipeline. 

[h1]Changes to Core Systems[/h1]

We have rebuilt all systems from the ground up to be more performant. As many gameplay systems as possible run on multiple threads. World streaming / loader, physics, networking, ballistics, movement, etc. all run in jobs. This release ships running a full client server architecture to allow for co-op in a later release.

notes.title: Upcoming changes with the Core Redesign Release - Post 4
notes.content:
[b]Update:[/b] We are still in the process of preparing the Core Redesign Release. We are have run into a few issues and are still putting on finishing touches. We will ship the release as soon as these issues are resolved. Thank you.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33892364/63a123c5cce304308cab60aa44fa534a42d3d198.png[/img]

Note: The Core Redesign Release has not yet been released.

[h1]Gameplay changes and improvements[/h1]

This post focuses on general gameplay changes coming with the Core Redesign Release and when we are planning on launching the Core Redesign Release. In addition to the areas discussed in prior posts and areas that will be explored in future posts, there are several keyways in which we are changing the game and its gameplay largely based off community feedback. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33892364/debfc63ff2859894a856b60081614bf324b9d166.jpg[/img]

We have completely overhauled and replaced the original map. The game’s map is now designed to be more interesting to navigate and be more conducive to creating interesting skirmishes and scenarios. Canyons are steeper and require more finesse to navigate. Obstacles require more complex problem solving to get around. Non-player characters (NPC)s wander up and down pathways where predators and bandits lay in wait. Exploration as a top tier gameplay element and challenge was in mind with the design of the new map.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33892364/afe665ca8a72a147ab02d53e03fff5832a3c90d9.jpg[/img]

Across the map camps of bandits and outlaws periodically form. These camps can be cleared out for loot and bounty prizes. These same outlaws attack the player and civilian NPCs as they wander the canyons and valleys of the map. As described in the post on NPC behavioral changes, these outlaws will enter standoffs and will wait to come out guns blazing until tensions flare or the player acts.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33892364/3ce6697969d1a8e57a203ab8f8f8e607b3fd4d38.jpg[/img]

The construct of playing as a U.S. Marshal is being removed in favor of allowing the player more freedom in how they choose their path. Robbing of town folks and cowboys will be allowed at the players own risk. A character selection system is being introduced to allow the player to choose from several characters. The characters pictured below are only some of the characters that the player can choose from. To spend money gained through the clearing of outlaws, robbing, and trading the player will be able to upgrade parts of a home ranch.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33892364/26209ac41b86b93fa7727a209d6b631bae3deb73.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33892364/84693e21c97c5fc5726df7362e5441c7f5a16bda.jpg[/img]

The survival elements of the game are also being revamped. Food and water consumption are no longer mandatory but are required for the replenishing and maintenance of the player’s health. Going long stretches without food or water will lower the player’s resistance to damage and increase the player’s risk of dying in combat. The player cannot die, however, from starvation or thirst.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33892364/ca3391a46f8745892e6525bafa9887c0c00ab413.png[/img]

[h1]When is the release launching?[/h1]

We feel that the Core Redesign Release is particularly important. The objective of the Core Redesign Release is to solve many of the bugs, low-level issues, and limitations that originally plagued the project. To this end the Core Redesign Release is an entire rewrite of the game’s code. Pretty much all systems, including animation, physics, input, character movement, NPC planning, the audio system interface, and rendering have been replaced or heavily overhauled.

 The new game code is a huge improvement over the code present in the old release and allows for improvements in all areas of the project. In addition to replacing the entire game’s code we have also overhauled or replaced most of the game’s assets (models, artwork, textures, etc).

We want there to be as few bugs and as much polish as we can practically get into this release. Changing engine features are allowing us to decrease the code’s complexity and increase the stability of this release. A new set of engine changes being released shortly will remove several low-level bugs and increase the quality of the release. To this end, we are shifting our release target to the end of January 2021 with the release tentatively planned to arrive in the last week of January.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33892364/171c4eb64ae55ef8adca75c9fa513b00ac1dd0c5.jpg[/img]

notes.title: Upcoming changes with the Core Redesign Release - Post 3
notes.content:
Note: The Core Redesign Release has not yet been released and is targeted to be released in late December.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33892364/3b6befe320011235d7a8272e1e7cffb720dbe775.jpg[/img]

This post focuses on the non-player character (NPC) and AI changes coming with the Core Redesign Release. Subsequent announcements will focus on other areas that the Core Redesign Release will change in the game. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33892364/debfc63ff2859894a856b60081614bf324b9d166.jpg[/img]

The systems dictating NPC behavior have been completely rewritten. NPC decision planning is now multithreaded and based on a utility system to allow for more complex behavior. Many of the changes to NPC behavior are based on user feedback. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33892364/f26bc0e6209282aa8930b4e9b94a0ba43b98cda3.jpg[/img]

Civilian NPCs will now wonder down paths instead of merely trekking through the woods. When crossing paths civilians will occasionally acknowledge each other as well as the player. Outlaws will setup choke points on paths and get in confrontations with civilians and cowboys.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33892364/91180391a42e0606ead1b4b1b595e06f7fb0f38a.jpg[/img]

Based on user feedback, NPCs no longer jump into gun battles at the first sight of an enemy, but instead enter a standoff. Standoffs will either resolve peacefully or turn into a battle when tensions flare. Standoffs will end peacefully when one of the parties involves backs away. If any parties involved move closer to their enemies it can trigger a fight. If neither party involved backs away, then eventually tensions will rise, and shooting will start.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33892364/2faee973e44f4dcf7443922e2b67c04cc7b22eb0.jpg[/img]

If the player wanders into the control zone of an NPC or a predatory animal, a standoff will begin until the player either leaves or a fight breaks out. By applying a brief standoff period when a NPC or a player confronts a predator, such as a wolf or bear, the player is given more warning and is better able to prepare for the impending attack.

notes.content:
Note: The Core Redesign Release has not yet been released and is targeted to ship in mid to late December.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33892364/a59dfb6607247345b9f8adda897072a5be550a36.png[/img]

This post focuses on the character movement changes coming with the Core Redesign Release. Subsequent announcements will focus on other areas that the Core Redesign Release will change in the game.

All the character movement systems have been completely overhauled. Character movements have been augmented to meet a few key goals: movement stability, movement fairness, and movement performance.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33892364/4b8383054b8b977c30fb4eeccb16bfcd4fd9ade3.png[/img]

To enforce movement stability, characters are now bound to the NavMesh. The NavMesh is a descriptor that defines where non playable characters (NPC) can travel in the world. The player is bound to the NavMesh except when airborne. When the player is falling, they are pulled back to the NavMesh. Why did we do this? First, this helps prevent instances where the player can fall through surfaces. Second, this helps prevents the player from ending up in places where they can become stuck. This leads to more stable movements and better immersion. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33892364/0a7af1349985d105c8eb896f10c0c079d875b250.png[/img]

Limiting the character to the NavMesh also enforces movement fairness. The player is now mostly constrained to areas where the NPCs can travel. This prevents odd situations where the player can go somewhere that an NPC cannot.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33892364/f678c1a6ccb2c721ed4c37f7901c6681a10d471d.png[/img]

Movement performance improvements come from two major places: multithreading and binding the player to the NavMesh. By locking the player to the NavMesh, we only need to query for collisions with other objects that move. This reduces the number of calculations needed to move the character. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33892364/171c4eb64ae55ef8adca75c9fa513b00ac1dd0c5.jpg[/img]

Character movement calculations and collision detection have been multithreaded (uses multiple CPU cores in parallel) to allow for more efficient processing. These performance improvements mean that more NPCs and animals can be spawned at once thus creating more complex scenarios. They also allow additional calculations and queries that allow players to move more realistic in response to the environment. For instance, character movement rates are reduced when travelling up a slope. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33892364/ca3391a46f8745892e6525bafa9887c0c00ab413.png[/img]

Subsequent announcements will focus on other areas that the Core Redesign Release will change in the game.

This post focuses on the graphical changes coming with the Core Redesign Release. Subsequent announcements will focus on other areas that the Core Redesign Release will change in the game. 
Graphics have been improved in several areas. As a basis we are using more advanced rendering features through a more advanced rendering pipeline. As seen in the comparisons below the new rendering tech allows for more realistic lighting and superior texture clarity.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33892364/7557529e204ad5259635538919334ae864fcb02a.jpg[/img]

Aliasing is less apparent, and colors are truer to life than before. Incorrect highlighting is reduced on the shadowed edge of objects. Contrast is improved. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33892364/8c54c3e7272df5b1d2c05411cdac341e385e97f0.png[/img]

The lighting is less harsh and does not washout key parts of the models anymore. Textures appear more realistic and vibrant. Shadows are deeper and more realistic.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33892364/72f16835a6677b23e3971a1ab237496de894fd38.png[/img]

Rasterization and antialiasing are sharper and more in focus. Objects are clearer and easier to identify.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33892364/c1c6b8fd9a2c27fdd48e30c612d72f75d9ed14f7.jpg[/img]

In addition to superior rendering tech, artwork has been replaced or remastered where necessary to make the game feel more realistic. Character models are more detailed and more realistic.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33892364/71f65188bcdf9adb122b872b25bed6665eb2e245.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33892364/9e224e04245302306d57c82c20a580d64ea98d2f.jpg[/img]

This is the first post of several detailing changes coming to the game.

notes.title: Sierra Madre: The Wild West 08/28/2019 Update
notes.content:
This release contains a number of bug fixes and stability improvements as well as a few new features.

[h1]New Features:[/h1]
[list]
[*] Native Americans Warriors will now spawn as you traverse the world and help you fight off bandits.
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/apps/970190/5986c0ca575e3de36202ead5bb9e6ec8fcb2cc19.jpg[/img]

[*] Added a quick loot ability. This will loot everything in a dead outlaw / animal inventory. This ability is activated by holding down the Action key (F by default key bindings) for 0.5 seconds while looking at a dead enemy.
[*] The weight limit on the player's inventory has been removed in favor of slowing the player down when carrying loads greater than 40 lbs.
[*] Restored dual pistol aiming while in first person mode. In third person mode right mouse button will fire the right weapon; left mouse button will fire the left weapon. In first person mode right mouse button will aim one of the revolvers and left mouse button will fire it.
[/list]

[h1]Changes:[/h1]
[list]
[*] Improved player grounding detection on slopes.
[*] Improved NPC behavior.
[*] Tweaked NPC accuracy at each difficulty level.
[*] Increased horse sprint / gallop times.
[*] Fixed issue where horse footprint sounds do not play.
[*] Fixed an issue where the player could become stuck sleeping / stuck in third person mode after sleeping.
[*] Improved NPC horse collision on NPC death (this should prevent horses from entering endless bucking loop).
[*] Fixed issue where characters and horses could be pushed through the terrain under certain circumstances.
[*] Switched from using animation events to timers for almost all weapon handling events. This should prevent endless readloading loops and the player getting stuck with a certain weapon.
[*] Added additional checks to prevent crashes in some circumstances on load.
[*] Horse now rotates independently of root motion. This should resolve issues where the horse will travel sideways.
[*] General performance improvements that help reduce lag.
[/list]

[h1]Known issues:[/h1]
[list]
[*] Occasionally, NPCs can become stuck while mounting / dismounting horses.
[*] In very rare circumstances the player can become stuck while mounting horses or using campfires. 
[/list]
Both of these issues are related to how animation events are fired and we are working to resolve these issues.

notes.title: Sierra Madre: The Wild West Core Stability Update
notes.content:
This update is primarily focused around fixing issues that were created in our creation of the core rewrite. We did, however, add birds that fly over head around the map.

[h1]Changes:[/h1]

[list]
[*] Collision detection improvements.

[*] Third person perspective melee hit detection improvements.

[*] First person perspective melee animations improved.

[*] Improved IK alignment for feet when going up steps on terrain.

[*] Fixed exception caused by pooled objects.

[*] Fixed issue with NPCs not successfully mounting horses.

[*] Fixed issues with NPCs flying sideways across the map.

[*] Improved lipsyncing for NPCs.

[*] Improved wagon turning animations.

[*] Improved Aiming IK for the player's character in third person perspective.

[*] Improved sprint animations in first person perspective.

[*] Fixed an issue where the camera can become wrongly aligned while riding the horse in first person perspective.

[*] Fixed an issue where towns people NPCs did not deal damaged consistently during fist fights.

[*] Fixed issues with the state system not always working as expected.

[*] Improved navigation with gamepads / keyboard in the inventory.

[*] Fixed issues with accessing items in the inventory.

[*] Fixed issues relating to IL2CPP compilation and runtime stability.

[*] Fixed issues where cloud quality settings did not apply until a restart.

[*] Fixed an issue where the player would become forced off his / her horse when taking damage.

[*] Fixed an issue where the player would jitter after being forced off of the horse.

[*] Improved horse auto steering.

[*] Improved an issue where punching when moving would leave the player unable to do anything.

[*] Tweaked horse and player stamina values.

[*] Increased the amount of time where the player can go without food and water.

[*] Fixed damage not always being applied when the player was out of food / water.

[*] Improved horse riding dismount reliability.

[*] Improved horse collision.

[*] Improve wagon driving.

[*] Improved NPC perception with better hearing.

[*] Add birds that fly around the map.
[/list]

[h1]Why somethings have not been seen to:[/h1]

Issues related to lighting have not been addressed in this update. Fixing shadow flickering issues on the current map requires making large compromises between the accuracy of shadows and the reduction of flickering.

In a future update we will be bringing a world generation system to [i]Sierra Madre[/i] that will allow us to better solve this issue. Although the engine behind this world generation system is fully functional, the world that it generates (the output) is still being designed. Once the world generation system is integrated we will upgrading [i]Sierra Madre[/i] to use Unity's [i]Scriptable Render Pipeline[/i], which will give us much finer control over the graphics in the game.

notes.title: Sierra Madre: The Wild West Core Rewrite Update
notes.content:
[b]Disclaimer:[/b] This update constitutes an overhaul of roughly 90% of our game's core source code and is a large change to the underlying systems of the game. Many of these changes are not aesthetically apparent. Over the next few updates we will be fundamentally changing the game's world (terrain, environment, etc), Core Gameplay, Rendering System (Lighting), and NPC behavior. This update, while rough in some areas, offers a new basis for the future development of Sierra Madre: The Wild West. The important thing is that this new core empowers us to provide more features in a much more manageable way.

Note: This release may not download immediately.

[h1]Changes:[/h1]

[b]Improved Character Controller[/b]

We have fully switched over to an advanced event-driven character controller. This character controller is more modular and is a huge improvement from a developer’s point of view. There are some rough edges. Animation transitions and blending require some tweaking and polish. These issues will solved in a future update. This controller is used to control the main character, NPCs, and horses. We will likely extend it to wildlife in a future update as well. This makes it easier for us to write behaviors that both the player and NPCs can utilize.

[b]Improved Animation System[/b]

We started this project as a first person shooter and as a result offered poor parity between first person and third person mode. To solve this we have introduced a new animation system that allows us to use the same animations between the first person and third person perspective. This new system also lays the groundwork for character customization (character customization is NOT in this update) by allowing us to easily swap out the rigs being used for the first person perspective. The third person and first person perspectives should now behave very similarly.

[b]Improved Gamepad Support[/b]

We have integrated a third party native control system that allows us to support many different gamepads. Most gamepads should work, but we have primarily targeted Xbox One controllers for this update. 

UI navigation has been improved for use with gamepads. The map UI has been tweaked to be controller friendly, but will be overhauled completely in a future update. The inventory UI has been completely overhauled. It has been designed with gamepad support in mind and has an acceptable amount of usability with a gamepad, but definitely needs some tweaking.

Menu UI has been tweaked both aesthetically and to better support gamepads, but some settings menus do not play nice with gamepads. The current Menu UI will be replaced in a future update.

[b]New Inventory System[/b]

We have overhauled the inventory system and replaced it with a robust, categorized inventory. The inventory now tracks all player possessions including weapons, ammo, horses, etc. The inventory can now be filtered based on category and can be used to call horses, access camp craft tools (bedrole, campfire), eat food, drink water, and equip weapons. Food and drink have been converted from using calories and fluid ounces as measurement units to being based on items. Where you used to have 64 fluid ounces of water, you now have one unit of water. Where you used to have 2000 calories of food, you now have 1 unit of meat (either raw or cooked). We will be expanding food groups to include more individual food items in future updates.

[b]New Interactions[/b]

New Interactions are discussed in this [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/970190/announcements/detail/1732104945948553484]development blog[/url].

[b]New Horse and Wagon Mechanics[/b]

We have replaced our old horse and wagon mechanics with new ones that are designed to require less direct steering. Horses and wagons will now try to avoid obstacles on their own. Instead of having to hold down a key to keep horses and wagons moving forward, you adjust speed by hitting the forward and backward movement keys (or moving the movement joystick in the forward or backward axes). This new system does have some issues on rough terrain, but this will be resolved when we overhaul our game world (which is one of our main focuses and we hope to have in the next feature update). 

[b]Horse Breeds[/b]

We now have different breeds of horses which can be bought at trading posts (will be moved to being bought at a livery stable in a future update).

[b]General Changes:[/b]
[list]

[*] Replaced tent with bedrole.

[*] Towns people now say greetings when approached.

[*] The player character now verbally indicates when they are hungry / thirsty.

[*] Added a Scoped .45-70 Breechloader.

[*] Added a Livery Stable to the tutorial.

[*] Improved blocking rain while inside buildings.

[*] Rewrote weapon mechanics. 

[*] Temporarily removed bullet drop.

[*] Temporarily removed hiring of lawmen.

[*] Added aim assist that automatically activates when a gamepad is in use and deactivates when the keyboard and mouse is in use.

[*] Added control hints that show which controls map to which functions. This can be disabled in the gameplay menu.

[*] Simplified gameplay settings options.

[*] Tweaked how long it takes to get hungry / thirsty.

[*] A direction indicator now indicates where attacks are coming from (only if cross hairs are enabled).

[*] New control remapping UI.

[*] New FPS arms model.

[*] Updated Tutorial to reflect changes.
[/list]

[b]Known issues:[/b]
[list]
[*] Horse speed and stamina values will show up with dollar signs in the inventory.

[*] Horses will buck and rear when ridden on unstable terrain. 

[*] Horses can start bucking uncontrollable when on really rough terrain. Dismounting the horse when it is in this state sometimes results in death.

[*] NPCs will sometimes become unresponsive. Sometimes NPCs will be found floating in mid air while on horse back.
 
[*] NPCs may become stuck on the edge of steep cliffs.

[*] Shadows will flicker when near the edge of the map (this will be resolved with the new world system).

[*] At certain times of day, faces that are not in direct sunlight will appear completely black (this will be addressed with the new render pipeline).

[*] Attempting to mount a wagon on the side of a cliff can result in the player becoming stuck. Rapidly hitting movement keys and the use key can sometimes unstuck the player.

[*] Exiting the inventory can sometimes result in the cursor being stuck on. Going back to the inventory and hitting escape to exit will resolve this.

[*] If you have the resolution of the game below your monitor’s native resolution, the native resolution may be restored when changing scenes. This may or may not be indicated in the graphics options.
[/list]

[b]What’s next?[/b]

We will now being focusing our development for the next feature updates on four key areas:

[list]
[*] Core Gameplay

[*] Fixing NPC behavior

[*] Upgrading to using the Scriptable Render Pipeline

[*] New World System
[/list]

notes.title: Sierra Madre: The Wild West Development Blog 03/29/2019
notes.content:
[h1]Moving to the Improved Character Controller, Input[/h1]

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/apps/970190/0f0581cb0636cf504db38a4f0aec11f6834c7ac3.jpg[/img]

Our integration to the improved character controller and input module is fully underway. Game-pad support is being vastly improved with the new input module and controls reporting is more aesthetically pleasing. The improved character controller offers more fluid movements and is much more flexible.

[h1]Better, Simpler Interactions and Controls[/h1]

As part of our move to the improved Character Controller, we have simplified interactions while also making interactions more interesting. Actions are now contextually based and as such there is no need for a permanent HUD bar.

Here are some screenshots of the new campfire interactions:

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/apps/970190/3c31813fd179bcae5a19f1fe04e22b8b710e71f0.jpg[/img]

notes.title: Sierra Madre: The Wild West Revised Roadmap 03/04/2019
notes.content:
[h1]Roadmap[/h1]

Thank you for your feedback. This roadmap is an [b]overview[/b] of planned features for the game based on user feedback. Please note that this is not finalized and is subject to change.

[list]
[*][b]Improved Core Architecture and Input System Migration[/b] We are working to migrate to a superior input module as well as improving the game's core architecture. The new input module should improve game-pad support.

[*][b]More Complex NPC Interactions[/b] We are working on adding meaningful interactions between the player and NPCs. These interactions will include simple dialogues and will vary by scenario.

[*][b]Factions and Public Opinion[/b] We are working on shaping the game to be based off of factions and a form of public opinion. We want your actions in the game to shape how NPCs react to you. We are also planning on allowing the player to choose / shape which faction they are a part of.

[*][b]Native Americans[/b] Native American artwork and NPC behavior is under development.

[*][b]Road Networks and Travelers[/b] We are planning on adding clearly defined trails to the game with wandering travelers, bandits that rob people, etc.

[*][b]NPC Recruiting / Hiring[/b] We are planning on allowing the player to hire NPCs to assist them in their adventures.

[*][b]Better Survival Equipment and Interactions[/b] We are working on adding more survival items. This will include individual foods, more tools, and more inventory items. We are also designing new interactions for existing and future tools. For example, we want to make tasks such as lighting a fire or cooking more interactive.

[*][b]Weapon Variety[/b] We will be adding more weapons / weapon variants to the game.

[*][b]Pick Your Own Adventure[/b] We want to give the player greater choice in what role they do in the game. We will be adding various activities or jobs that will shape the player's role. We would like to add tasks like farming, shipment escorting, ranching, buying properties, etc.

[*][b]More Activities and Scenarios / Missions[/b] We are planning on expanding the number of activities in the game. We would like to add activities such as rodeos, ranch management, farming, gambling, etc. We are also designing various scenarios / additional missions.

[*][b]Character Customization[/b] We are planning on adding some form of character customization to the game.

[*] [b]Improved Graphics and Lighting[/b] With the release of Unity 2019.1, we will be migrating to a new and improved graphics rendering module.

[*][b]Injury Mobility Limitations[/b] Currently the player decreased vision when hurt. We would like to extend this to include limitations based on injuries to certain body parts. For example, if the player is shot in the leg they should move slower.

[*][b]Saddle Bags, Stashes, and Inventory Improvements[/b] We are planning to add features such as saddle bags, saddle holsters, and loot stashes where gear can be stored.

[*][b]More, better sound effects[/b] We are planning on improving our sound effects and adding more sound effects.

[*][b]Mac & Linux (Debian) Support[/b] We would like to have full Mac, Linux, and Windows 10 cross-platform support. Note: we only intend on supporting x64 versions of these operating systems.

[*][b]Better Wildlife[/b] Better wildlife are under development to ensure a more realistic experience.

[*][b]Better Artwork[/b] We are currently overhauling our animals, character art, and other game assets to be more realistic.

[*][b]Better In-game UI[/b] We will be making the user interface easier to use, more aesthetically pleasing, and more compatible with game-pads.

[*][b]More Maps[/b] We have a series of maps planned that are currently under development.
[/list]

[h1]Being Researched, To Be Determined[/h1]

These features are being researched as possible additions to the game.

[list]
[*] [b]A Separate Multiplayer / Co-op Game Mode[/b] The addition of a multiplayer mode depends on a lot of factors and will only be done after we have created a solid single-player experience. Any addition of multiplayer / co-op would be treated as a separate game mode and [b]will not effect the single-player game mode[/b].

That being said, the changes we are making to the game's core architecture have been designed with networking in mind. We are designing the game to allow for the addition of a separate multiplayer mode.

[*] [b]Basic Modding Support[/b] Mods support is under research and the extent of what kinds of mods could / should be added to the game is still being determined.
[/list]

notes.title: Sierra Madre: The Wild West Development Blog 2/21/2019
notes.content:
We have been working on a number of internal improvements to the game's architecture to facilitate new features.

[h1]New Character Art[/h1]

We are overhauling all character art in the game. A preview of this character art has already been rolled out to the gunslinger NPCs.

[h1]New Town Layouts and Building Art[/h1]

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/apps/970190/437cb8c87adc1b63064017d9089ff4ee5579e0e4.jpg[/img]

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/apps/970190/97653bb474b46cbc839fcf881c3a3a1ebb6287c6.jpg[/img]

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/apps/970190/3e1933a1b4ce1b818747ebccb0bd8848b64c7251.jpg[/img]

We are overhauling our buildings with models that are both more realistic, higher quality, and more efficient to render. We hope to have the new building art in the next update coming soon. The new building models use typically a third of the polygons and at least half of the texture memory of the old building models.

[h1]New Factions and NPC Behavior[/h1]

We are working on a new American Indian Faction as well as overhauling the current NPC behavior. The new NPC behavior will focus on creating more interesting scenarios and adding interactions with NPCs. The new system is being previewed with the gunslinger NPCs in the game. This system will be brought to the other NPCs soon.

[h1]New Character Controller and Other Foundational Improvements[/h1]

[b]Migrating to a better character controller[/b]

We have begun internally migrating over to an improved character controller. The character controller is responsible for moving the player, handling weapon mechanics, animating the player's model, and handling interactions between the player and objects in the world.

Fortunately, our game's core architecture uses a loosely-coupled, modular design and will allow us to migrate to this new system without breaking important functionality.

[b]Why are we migrating to a new character controller?[/b]

Well, the character controller that we currently use in game was rigidly designed and is not modular enough to handle some of the new features and interactions we are working on.

Instead of rewriting parts of the core character controller every time we need to add functionality for new features, we have decided to migrate to a modular and flexible controller. A modular character controller makes it easier for us to write interactions and to add new features.

[b]Input system improvements and better interactions[/b]

As part of this migration effort we are moving to a new native input module and looking to simplify input in the game. The new native input module will have better support for game pads (e.g. XBox controllers).

We are also working on simplifying complex interactions and making basic tasks more interesting.

[b]Moving weapons into the inventory[/b]

Currently weapons are managed outside of the inventory. We are working to migrate weapons to being stored in the inventory and to being treated as inventory items. Moving the weapons into the inventory will allow us to improve aspects of game-play related to weapon selection and picking up and dropping weapons. One such aspect is allowing the player to customize the game's HUD bar to include the tools / weapons that they want to have quick access to.

[b]How these changes affect the development of the game[/b]

These foundational changes are aimed at making development of new features easier as well as improving general game-play. Once we have completed and integrated these foundational changes we will be better able to design and implement user feature requests.

notes.title: Sierra Madre: The Wild West User Feedback Update 1
notes.content:
Build 3418701

This update incorporates some minor improvements and a new feature suggested in user feedback. 

[b]Wood Chopping[/b]

Gathering fire wood no longer consists of searching the ground looking for sticks. Now you can gather fire wood by simply walking up to a tree and chopping the tree with your knife or hatchet. 

The knife will gather a stick of wood for every third hit to a tree and can gather up to three sticks of wood per tree. The hatched will gather a stick of wood for every hit to a tree and can gather up to nine sticks of wood per tree.

[b]Improvements[/b]
[list]
[*] We have added some more steam achievements. Note: if you are currently on one of the missions that has one of theses achievements, the achievement will not take effect until you have completed the mission a second time.

[*] The enemy AI is now way less aggressive, doesn't jump around as much, deals less damage, and has lower accuracy. 

[*] The enemy AI now loses sight of the player more quickly and forgets the player sooner.

[*] Increased enemy loot lifetime.

[*] The player's health now auto-regenerates up to 66% a few seconds after being damaged instead of only regenerating up to 25%.

[*] Ambient audio is now always controlled by the ambient audio slider.

[*] An issue where water splashes were heard for no reason should now be resolved.

[*] Player now gathers wood using chopping of trees instead of picking up sticks.

[*] We reduced the brightness of sun shafts and toned down the overall brightness of the sun.

[*] Horses now have greater stamina and can gallop for greater distances.

[*] The player's horse now has twice the hit points and is harder to kill in combat.

[*] Tweaked spawning of enemies to reduce instances were huge mobs of outlaws are attacking the player.

[*] Increased piano's volume in the bar and tied the piano's volume to the music audio channel. 

[*] Fixed the pianist's rag doll to not fall through the bench when killed.
[/list]

[b]The Next Feature Update[/b]

Things discussed below this point will be in the next feature update to the game and are not in today's update.

The next feature update will focus on improving the user interface, making in game interactions more intuitive, and improving the game play aspects of the game.

The next feature update will include the following improvements:
[list]

[*] An improved and simplified inventory / store system.

[*] A better in-game map.

[*] Game play related settings options including gamma correction, mouse invert, enemy AI difficulty, survival difficulty, a difficulty preset, and in game HUD settings.

[*] An optional HUD that will include things such as a mini-map, horse stamina read outs, and other things to help you navigate the world and survive.

[*] A new 3D, interactive tutorial. The current tutorial is, in a word, bad. We are going to replace it with a tutorial that actually has you do things to learn how to do them.

[*] New enemy AI spawning rules that will make the game more interesting and less repetitive.

[*] Better game play elements.

[*] Introduce graphics settings to help with flickering in buildings.
[/list]

We value your opinions and feedback, so please let us know how we can improve the game and things that you would like to do in the game.

Please post any feature requests for the next feature update as well as any issues with today's update in the comments below.

notes.title: Improved Horse Mechanics
notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/apps/970190/23465ad9fa786297c6e5fd89b39e92c12a739fd2.jpg[/img]

We have introduced several improvements to [i]Sierra Madre: The Wild West[/i]'s horse mechanics. Along with bug fixes, we have introduced an important new mechanic: horse ownership. Previously, the player owned the last horse they rode, but this is no longer the case. Now, the player starts the game owning a horse and this horse goes with the player throughout the world.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/apps/970190/ed2d9d5eb4b8f928860fb367e47d0c151a1c0062.jpg[/img]

The player's horse follows them around the map maintaining a following distance of 30 to 50 meters. The player can call their horse and it will run to the player's side.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/apps/970190/175cdea3178de6dad133750b539706a0c09b4440.jpg[/img]

The player can ride other horses or wagons and their loyal horse will continue following them. This was designed so that the player would have their horse nearby even as the player does long journeys for missions.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/apps/970190/dcc9374354630feffcd89c6eef03e78fcb40dd7c.jpg[/img]

When the player loads their game, their horse will spawn with them near their tent. This is the case no matter where the player left their horse unless their horse was killed.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/apps/970190/7a9780079c57afbd2383cbb982a34c7ec3ab6762.jpg[/img]

In the event that the player's horse is killed, the player can buy a new horse at the trading post. Eventually we hope to add a horse taming mechanic to the game. If the player already owns a living horse and they buy another one, the new horse will become their owned horse and the old horse will cease to follow the player.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/apps/970190/50ba9f7d2aabe06961747fcd14458189e8b61d34.jpg[/img]

If the player's horse is killed and the player has not purchased a new horse, then they will not spawn with a horse when loading their game. 

In addition to horse ownership, horses now move slower as they become tired. If the player runs their horse over a great distance they will have to let their horse rest or walk for the horse to regain its energy.

What do you guys think of the new horse mechanics? 

Please post any suggestions or questions in the comments below.

notes.title: Early Access Release Date Clarification
notes.content:
We have always planned on releasing [i]Sierra Madre[/i] to early access as close to the middle of December as possible, but we haven't clearly defined this on our store page before. We want to be as transparent about the development of [i]Sierra Madre[/i] as possible and would like to clarify when we intend to release this project to early access.

To clarify this we have updated the store page to now say mid-December, which was always the intended date. We don't want to lock it down to a specific date quite yet as we have a few things we want to polish.

We intend on releasing [i]Sierra Madre[/i] to Early Access between December 14th and December 21st with December 14th being preferred.

[b]Why mid-December instead of a specific day?[/b]

We want to make each release (including the first) as bug free as possible and want the flexibility to make sure that this happens. At this point we only have a few known issues that need addressing. 

We also have two more features left on our list we want to get in this release: improved horse mechanics and improved weapons models and animations for the player character. These two additions are on schedule and shouldn't hold up the release, but in the event that an unforeseen problem arises we want the flexibility to solve it.

Thank you for your patience and interest.

notes.title: Missions and Objectives Added To Sierra Madre
notes.content:
[b]Missions and Objectives[/b]

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/apps/970190/795332bd050211894cf0575b3f26ad650fe5a23c.jpg[/img]

[i]Sierra Madre[/i]'s mission system is now up and running. The mission system allows the player to complete mini-missions / quests for in game cash. These missions are designed to help the player to explore the map and travel great distances. All missions have rewards proportional to their difficultly and the distance they require the player to travel. 

In the first early access release of [i]Sierra Madre[/i] there will only be three different mission types: [i]Delivery[/i], [i]Outlaw Hunter[/i], and [i]Town Liberator[/i]. In the [i]Delivery[/i] mission the player must drive a wagon from the town they are in to another town or trading post on the map. In the [i]Outlaw Hunter[/i] mission the player must travel to the location marked on their map and take out the outlaw there. In the [i]Town Liberator[/i] mission the player must kill all outlaws around the town or trading post that the outlaws are harassing. More mission types are planned for future updates after the first early access release.

To select a mission the player must go to the nearest Sheriff's station (which was suggested in this [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/970190/discussions/0/1741100729946486364/]post[/url]) and select one of the missions from the board.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/apps/970190/036b6d111bb32296af5191542c1323fc1e383bb7.jpg[/img]

When the player is near the board and looking at a mission a description will pop up. After the player has selected a mission, an objective display will appear in the top left hand corner of the screen.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/apps/970190/fc6aad5c7813ce8f282870a4891f01cb075a0294.jpg[/img]

The mission's objectives will continue appearing as the player progresses through the mission.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/apps/970190/ca8802abc66c9d10e4c1c27ca4e4627176226f80.jpg[/img]

Once the player has completed all of the objectives in the mission a completion banner will appear and the in game cash reward will be added to the player's inventory. 

What do you guy's think about the new mission system? Any ideas for improvements? What missions would you like to see in future updates? 

Please let us know in the comments below.

notes.title: Improved Survival Elements
notes.content:
Our survival elements were, in a word, lacking. Since we are making a survival games this was quite a problem. So we decided to add more survival mechanics to [i]Sierra Madre[/i]! We have divided food and water into two categories: edible/potable and inedible/non-potable. When you collect food from animals or collect water from streams or lakes it is not safe to drink or eat. You can eat or drink it, but you [i]might[/i] fall ill and loose some of health after eating or drinking it. The effects of consuming unsafe water or food are not immediately felt. It might be an hour before these effects are felt.

So if the basic food and water that is collected is now unsafe how do you go about surviving? With fire!

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/apps/970190/4710d77ba96396696217ae6279bc3c18b3c843a1.jpg[/img]

The camp fire is a new tool that can be used to sterilize food and water. The camp fire can be placed at any time and most anywhere. Once a camp fire has been placed you must add wood to it and light it (wood can be gathered around the map or bought from trading posts). Once the fire is lit you can add food and water to be sterilized. The food and water will cook for a certain amount of time and will be automatically added to your inventory once cooked.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/apps/970190/42c6e89448a35c876c4296d76c2d065e3e49933c.jpg[/img]

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/apps/970190/e60a7aab3fa32cc1556b7848d45c1e46b1bbd163.jpg[/img]

What do y'all think?

notes.title: Sierra Madre Early Access Release Improvements and Upgrades
notes.content:
As part of our continuing effort to make [i]Sierra Madre[/i] the best game possible, we are upgrading some of our assets and technologies before our first release.

[b]Better Player Character and Weapon Artwork[/b]

The first major improvement we are making is in terms of aesthetics: better quality weapons and arm models for the player character. We are replacing our current weapon models with more authentic weapons and using a higher quality mesh for our main character. Here are a few of the weapon models we will be using:

[IMG]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steam/apps/970190/ss_10d6cc7acc1ec1223eb742546292e65bc3cb9936.1920x1080.jpg?t=1541521749[/img]

[b]Smarter Enemies, Allies, and Wildlife[/b]

In addition to our weapon art improvements, we are also overhauling our current Artificial Intelligence (A.I.) system. More specifically, we are replacing two separate A.I. systems with a unified system based off of Utility theory.

Well, that's cool, but why you should care? Our new Utility driven A.I. empowers enemies, allies, and wildlife to make more intelligent, less repetitive decisions all while reducing overhead. Immersion and realism are significantly improved over what is currently shown in our game trailer.

[b]More Things To Do[/b]

We are adding a new mission system that will supply the player with specific objectives to complete. Completing these objectives will grant the user rewards and makes the game much more interesting.

[b]Performance Improvements[/b]

Upgrading the game engine version has yielded significant performance improvements. Physics has seen a roughly 2x performance boost and multi-core processors see better utilization. 

We have also upgraded to a new, multi-threaded vegetation rendering system that offers unbelievable performance! In our testing, [i]Sierra Madre[/i] was running on Ultra settings, 4k resolution @ 70 to 90 frames per second (using a Nvidia GTX 1080 graphics card)*.

Finally, we are switching to using a multi-threaded IK system that makes the aiming animations of enemies and allies significantly faster and more realistic looking.

*End user performance may vary depending on system.
